title: Synergistic Effect of Profiled Spacers and Membrane Surface Modification in Desalination Processes in Electromembrane Systems: Mathematical Modeling
content: Concentration polarization at the surface of ion-exchange membranes limits the rate of mass transfer and determines the energy consumption of electrodialysis. Turbulence-promoting spacers and profiling of the membrane surface are the two traditional remedies; however, they are almost always considered separately, and non-conducting spacers shade the membrane and increase the channel resistance. In this work, a two-dimensional mathematical model of ion transport in a flow-through desalination channel is developed on the basis of the coupled Nernst–Planck–Poisson and Navier–Stokes equations in the potentiodynamic mode. Using the Poisson equation instead of the local electroneutrality assumption makes it possible to account for the space-charge region and describe electroconvection "from first principles." Eight channel configurations were compared: a smooth or structured cation-exchange membrane, with or without profiled spacers placed in various positions. It is shown that the structured surface and profiled spacers act synergistically: the spacers direct the solution from the flow core toward the membrane's developed surface relief, and the overall benefit exceeds the sum of the individual effects. The combined design raises the limiting current by a factor of about 1.4, shortens the limiting-current plateau, increases the current at 1.4 V by 40–45%, provides a 35% increase of the active membrane area, a 40% reduction of concentration polarization, a 28% acceleration of desalination, a ×1.5 increase of the ion flux, and a 15% reduction of the working voltage. The main conclusion agrees with an independent 3D multiphysics study supported by experiments with physically manufactured profiled membranes.
